sentences.text: This dinosaur possessed a skull measuring 18 centimeters long and an estimated total body length of 2.5 meters.
The dinosaur was discovered near the locality of Balde de Leyes in the Caucete Department of San Juan Province.
Leyesaurus was first named by Cecilia Apaldetti, Ricardo N. Martinez, Oscar A. Alcober, and Diego Pol in 2011.
The genus name honors the Leyes family, who lived in Balde de Leyes and discovered the holotype fossil — the specimen the species is based on.
The species name marayensis refers to the Marayes-El Carrizal Basin where the holotype was found.
Leyesaurus is classified within the class Saurischia.
Leyesaurus belongs to the family Massospondylidae.
Within the family Massospondylidae, Leyesaurus is most closely related to the genus Adeopapposaurus.
Leyesaurus fossils were found in the Quebrada del Barro Formation, which dates to the Lower Jurassic period.
Leyesaurus lived during the Hettangian to Toarcian stages, between 201.4 and 174.7 million years ago.
